title: After entering an option with the keyboard in a multiselect, the cursor is positioned at the beginning of the multiselect
body: ### Checklist - [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues. - [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue. - [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue. ### Summary After entering an option with the keyboard in a multiselect, the cursor is placed at the beginning of the multiselect (and not after the selected options). As a result, when typing the next option, it is difficult to read what is being typed. ### Reproducible Code Example [![Open in Streamlit Cloud](https://static.streamlit.io/badges/streamlit_badge_black_white.svg)](https://issues.streamlitapp.com/?issue=gh-16133) ```Python import streamlit as st options = st.multiselect( "What are your favorite colors?", ["Green", "Yellow", "Red", "Blue"], default=[], ) st.write("You selected:", options) ``` ### Steps To Reproduce 1. Click on the multiselect. 1. Type "Red" and press [ENTER] (the cursor is now after the selected color) 1. Press [ESC] once (to close the list of options) and then press [ESC] again (to clean the selection) 1. Type "Red" and press [ENTER] ### Expected Behavior The cursor is again after the selected color (Red) ### Current Behavior The cursor is at the beginning of the multiselect. It is difficult to read what is being typed now. ### Is this a regression? - [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version. ### Debug info - Streamlit version: 1.60.0 - Python version: 3.14 - Browser: Edge, Opera, Firefox ### Additional Information _No response_
